investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm); the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for ~139–145 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a full contract-gap failure. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no allocatable slots for new probe pods at the time of the eval run.

[Likely] The cluster has only 2 nodes configured with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and the pod's node affinity/selector restricts scheduling to exactly those nodes, meaning any saturation of that resource causes a total scheduling blackout.

[Possible] A recent scale-down, node failure, or maintenance event reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent probe and production workloads simultaneously.

[Possible] The pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm is set to a quantity that cannot be satisfied even when one slot is nominally free (e.g., request > 1 unit per pod and only fractional capacity remains).
[Lower confidence] A misconfiguration in node affinity/selector rules is excluding nodes that should be eligible, artificially shrinking the schedulable pool to only the 2 already-saturated nodes.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-07-07T06:02–06:07Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the eval's remote-agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never schedules, the agent is never created, and the eval runner never reaches the state-polling step, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for the peer-pod VM type required by remote agents. The eval runner calls createAgent(..., "remote", ...) at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905, which submits the pod; the pod remains Unschedulable for ~145 s before the check times out. Because the agent pod never starts, the runner cannot collect orgId, agentId, readyState, or state, causing the contract validation error "Missing expected evidence: orgId, agentId, readyState, state". This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm); the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for ~139–145 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a full contract-gap failure. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no allocatable slots for new probe pods at the time of the eval run.

[Likely] The cluster has only 2 nodes configured with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and the pod's node affinity/selector restricts scheduling to exactly those nodes, meaning any saturation of that resource causes a total scheduling blackout.

[Possible] A recent scale-down, node failure, or maintenance event reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent probe and production workloads simultaneously.

[Possible] The pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm is set to a quantity that cannot be satisfied even when one slot is nominally free (e.g., request > 1 unit per pod and only fractional capacity remains).
[Lower confidence] A misconfiguration in node affinity/selector rules is excluding nodes that should be eligible, artificially shrinking the schedulable pool to only the 2 already-saturated nodes.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-07-07T06:02–06:07Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the eval's remote-agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never schedules, the agent is never created, and the eval runner never reaches the state-polling step, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for the peer-pod VM type required by remote agents. The eval runner calls createAgent(..., "remote", ...) at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905, which submits the pod; the pod remains Unschedulable for ~145 s before the check times out. Because the agent pod never starts, the runner cannot collect orgId, agentId, readyState, or state, causing the contract validation error "Missing expected evidence: orgId, agentId, readyState, state". This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 are already full. This is a configuration constraint that limits the effective scheduling pool to 2 nodes, amplifying any capacity pressure.

The runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) but a prior interrupted run may not have completed cleanup.

Cluster node pool under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may not have enough total VM slots to handle simultaneous remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime eval pods if they run in parallel or overlap with production workloads.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Swarm Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or exercising the runtime, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes resource constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler reports 0/6 nodes available: 2 nodes have Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable (no preemption victims found, preemption not helpful). The pod remained Unschedulable for ~145 seconds before the eval timed out, preventing agent creation entirely and leaving all required evidence fields unpopulated.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId — pod scheduling is the first blocking step before any evidence can be gathered.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the check failed well within that window at 149514ms, confirming the failure is scheduling-driven not a latency threshold breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots on the peer-pods-capable nodes are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. If the affinity were broader, other nodes might absorb the pod.

Tertiary — concurrent eval runs or other workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously: if multiple eval runs or production workloads are scheduled at the same time, the finite VM quota on peer-pods nodes could be transiently exhausted.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be permanently insufficient for the expected eval concurrency, requiring node pool scaling.

recommendedNextActions: Investigate current kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the two affinity-matching nodes in the production-api cluster to determine whether the exhaustion is transient (concurrent workloads) or persistent (under-provisioning).
Identify which workloads are consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the eligible nodes and whether any can be evicted or rescheduled to free capacity for eval pods.

Review the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector to determine whether the 4 non-matching nodes could be made eligible (e.g., by adding the required label or relaxing the selector), which would expand the schedulable pool beyond the 2 currently eligible nodes.
Check whether the cluster autoscaler is configured to scale the kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable node pool and, if so, why it did not scale up before the eval timed out at ~145s.
Re-run all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) after any capacity remediation to confirm recovery and collect the required evidence fields.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false (infra/evals/status/features.json line 185), so its failure alone does not trigger a feature outage; however, remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true and their simultaneous failure (sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) may contribute to a degraded or outage status for the remote-agents feature depending on the degradedAfterFailures=1 / outageAfterFailures=2 thresholds.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime that produces a scheduled pod and returns all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) would disprove that the scheduling failure is persistent.

kubectl describe nodes output showing non-zero allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity remaining on the two affinity-matching nodes at the time of the failure would suggest the scheduler message was transient or erroneous.
Evidence that the pod was eventually scheduled but the agent runtime returned an empty or malformed response would shift the root cause from scheduling exhaustion to a runtime or API-layer defect.

A passing run of the local-agent-runtime check (which uses a different machine type and does not require kata.peerpods.io/vm) at the same time would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote/peer-pods scheduling layer and not a broader API or auth outage.

Cluster autoscaler logs showing a scale-up event that resolved the kata.peerpods.io/vm shortage shortly after the eval run would indicate a transient capacity gap rather than a permanent under-provisioning.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct check rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), alerting when the schedulable pool shrinks.

Add a remote-agent scheduling latency eval with a tighter warning threshold (e.g., 30s) to catch pod scheduling delays before they reach the full 145s timeout, enabling earlier detection of capacity pressure.

Add a sibling-correlation eval that fires a single 'shared scheduling dependency' alert when all checks under remote-agents fail with the same Unschedulable message, reducing alert noise and making the cluster-level cause immediately visible.
